"### Chart Description: Goods Trade Balance

The chart illustrates the developments in the goods trade balance, exports, and imports from August 2017 to April 2024. Values are expressed in **Billions of US$**, as a **3-month moving average (3m m.a.)**, and are **Seasonally Adjusted (S.A.)**.

#### **Axes and Legend**
*   **Left Y-Axis (LHS):** Measures value for Exports and Imports, ranging from **2 to 10** billion US$.
*   **Right Y-Axis (RHS):** Measures the Trade Balance, ranging from **-2 to 4** billion US$.
*   **X-Axis:** Timeline from **Aug-17 to Apr-24**.
*   **Data Series:**
    *   **Exports:** Light blue line (LHS).
    *   **Imports:** Dark blue line (LHS).
    *   **Trade Balance (rhs):** Gray vertical bars (RHS).

---

#### **Key Data Points and Trends**

| Time Period | Exports (LHS) | Imports (LHS) | Trade Balance (RHS) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Aug-17 (Start)** | ~4.8 | ~5.5 | ~-0.7 (Deficit) |
| **Oct-18** | ~5.1 | ~4.8 | ~0.3 (Turning to surplus) |
| **Late 2019** | ~5.9 | ~3.7 | ~+2.3 (Peak surplus period) |
| **Mid-2020** | ~4.5 | ~3.0 (Lowest) | ~+1.5 (Surplus) |
| **Mar-22** | ~7.8 (Peak) | ~7.2 | ~+0.6 (Surplus) |
| **Aug-22** | ~7.2 | ~7.6 (Peak) | ~-0.4 (Deficit) |
| **Jun-23** | ~5.5 | ~6.8 | ~-1.4 (Deepest deficit) |
| **Apr-24 (End)** | ~6.3 | ~4.9 | ~+1.4 (Return to surplus) |

#### **Summary of Trends:**
*   **Trade Balance:** The trade balance was mostly in deficit from late 2017 to late 2018. It experienced a sustained period of surplus from 2019 through late 2022. A significant deficit occurred throughout most of 2023, reaching a low of approximately **-$1.4 billion** in June 2023. By early 2024, it recovered to a surplus of roughly **+$1.4 billion**.
*   **Exports:** Peaked in early 2022 at approximately **$7.8 billion**. Following a sharp decline in 2023 (bottoming around **$5.5 billion**), they have shown a recent recovery toward **$6.3 billion**.
*   **Imports:** Reached their highest point in August 2022 at approximately **$7.6 billion**. Since mid-2023, there has been a sharp contraction, falling below **$5 billion** by April 2024."
